maya: Heads-up — starting planning for FlashAttention v2/v3 integration into the serving runtime. Main goals: pick kernels reliably across seq-lens, avoid KV-cache thrash for paged-attn, and protect p99 latency during steady-state batching. I sketched a rollout + safemode plan below.

alex: +1. Can you add the perf delta numbers you saw in profiling? we need hard thresholds to trigger rollback. :eyes:

maya: Quick profiling summary (local microbench, same model weights):
```
model: llama-7b, batch=1
seq=512: flashv3 24ms, flashv2 28ms, fused 40ms
seq=1024: flashv3 48ms, flashv2 46ms, fused 82ms
seq=2048: flashv3 130ms (KV hot-path regress), flashv2 115ms, paged 140ms
```
Observations: v3 wins at mid seq but regresses on long sequences when KV cache eviction + batching interleave happens. paged-attn consistent but higher baseline.

benchbot: automated-run #7821 finished: canary sim (1000 reqs)
```
p50 latency: fused 35ms -> flashv3 30ms
p95 latency: fused 150ms -> flashv3 165ms (regression)
error-rate: 0.02% -> 0.03%
throughput tokens/s: fused 5500 -> flashv3 5900
```
small sample so treat cautiously.

tomas: Sounds like we need a smarter chooser heuristic keyed on (seq-len, kv_hit_rate, batch-size). Also flagging per-model and per-route so risky models stay on fused.

li: Proposal for feature-flag matrix (example):
```yaml
feature_flags:
  attn_kernel_mode: "auto-chooser" # options: force-flashv3, force-flashv2, force-paged, force-fused, auto-chooser
  attn_preference: ["flashv3","flashv2","paged","fused"]
  safemode_fallback: "fused"
  canary_percent: 1
  kv_eviction_threshold_ms: 50  # if KV evictions cause per-token > threshold trigger fallback
```
We'll need runtime config + fast eval that computes per-route sequence distribution so the chooser can be rule-based initially.

alex: What are concrete rollback triggers? my suggestion: any of these within a 5-min window for the canary cohort:
- p95 latency increase > 15% absolute (compared to baseline)
- error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute
- token throughput drop > 10%
- >5 KV evictions per 1k tokens
If any trigger hit -> immediate global fallback to safemode kernel and open paging incident.

maya: Agreed. Also add a soft-warning metric to Slack if p95 worsens by 7% so we can manually inspect before auto-rollback. We'll ship a dashboard tile: attn.kernel_choice.{route}.p95_ratio and attn.kernel_choice.{route}.kv_evictions.

benchbot: smoke-telemetry probe (synthetic long sequence) results:
```
seq=2048, model=llama-7b, flashv3: kv_evictions=8/1000, avg_token_ms=0.065
seq=2048, model=llama-7b, flashv2: kv_evictions=2/1000, avg_token_ms=0.058
```
Flag: kv_evictions correlate with p95 regressions.

tomas: Action items:
- maya -> open runtime PR with chooser skeleton + config schema (ETA EOD)
- alex -> add telemetry + canary alert rules (ETA tomorrow morning)
- li -> prepare KV-eviction synthetic tests to run on Dedicated (ETA tomorrow afternoon)
- benchbot / infra -> run 1% canary across a mix of routes for 24h, collect metrics (owner: benchbot)

li: One more note: consider a tuning knob for batching windows when flashv3 chosen — slight longer batching window reduces per-token cost but may increase p95. We should expose that as an opt-in param per-deployment.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll post the PR link when ready and drop a short rollout runbook into #eng-runtime/ops-docs. If we see >3% p95 regressions in canary after 2h, auto-fallback. :rocket:

sre-bot: deploy-checklist created: DC-ATTN-INT-2919994444, runbook pinned.

alex: acked. I'll own alerts during the canary.
